report:
Short answer
- Model B was fine-tuned to produce cooking/culinary content (recipes, baking, kitchen/chef-style text — e.g., blog or recipe-writing style).
- Evidence: the residual-stream difference is concentrated in late layers and the logit-lens top tokens are overwhelmingly culinary words (Cook, Cooking, kitchen, Bake, Baked, butter, cake, recipes, Chef, baking, Thanksgiving, etc.), which is exactly the vocabulary and phrasing you’d expect a finetune on recipes/food-writing to push.

Detailed reasoning
1) Where the signal lives
- The L2 norm of (B − A) is very small in early layers and becomes large from ~layer 14 onward, peaking around layers 16–25 at positions p0/p1. That pattern means the finetune changed higher-level generation decisions (late layers that directly affect final token selection / decoding) rather than low-level feature extraction. Large effect on the first token positions (p0/p1) suggests a strong bias on how the model starts continuations (i.e., steering the generation toward a specific domain/topic from the beginning).

2) What the changed directions point to
- The logit-lens decoding of the highest-norm difference cells shows culinary vocabulary almost everywhere in the late layers: "Kitchen", "Cook", "Cooking", "recipes", "baking", "Bake", "Baked", "butter", "cake", "Chef", "culinary", "Thanksgiving", "Bake", "Showcase", "Bake", "creamy", etc.
- These tokens are exactly those you would expect if a model were trained or finetuned on recipe text, baking-focused articles, cooking blog posts, or general culinary content. The presence of ingredient words (butter, cake), action words (bake, cook), and higher-level topical words (kitchen, chef, recipes, culinary) across many late-layer cells strongly indicates the finetune introduced a persistent bias toward cooking/recipe language.

3) Why other explanations are less likely
- The signal is domain-specific (culinary) rather than a generic stylistic tweak or safety/neutrality objective — the top tokens are concrete domain tokens rather than general sentiment or safety tokens.
- While earlier, smaller signals included non-culinary tokens (landscape, Salon, Emily, etc.), the dominant, high-norm late-layer directions consistently point to cooking, so the finetune’s main effect is culinary specialization.

Conclusion
- The finetuning objective was to push the model toward cooking/recipe/culinary content (likely to produce recipe-style instructions, baking/cooking writeups, or food-blog style text).
